title: Alkanes and alkenes: the bromine water test
examples: What is the difference between alkanes and alkenes?
How do you test for an alkene?

explain.say: Two families of hydrocarbons look almost the same on paper. But one simple test tells them apart in seconds! Look at the board. You can see alkanes on one side and alkenes on the other.

draw.text: Alkanes and alkenes: the bromine water test

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The double bond is the difference

explain.say: See the alkanes? All their carbon atoms are joined by single bonds. We call them saturated, which means they hold as many hydrogen atoms as possible. Methane, in cooking gas, and ethane are alkanes. What do you think unsaturated means?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The double bond is the difference

explain.say: It means there is room for more! Look at the alkenes. They have a double bond between two carbon atoms, written C=C. That double bond can open up and grab other atoms. Ethene is the simplest alkene. How many carbons do you think ethene has?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: The double bond is the difference

explain.say: Two! Now here is the test. Look at the board. Shake orange bromine water with an alkane, and it stays orange. Shake it with an alkene, and it goes colourless, because the bromine adds across the double bond. Why do you think sunflower oil is in the second group?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What happens to orange bromine water?

explain.say: Because plant oils are unsaturated! Brilliant. Wow: some margarine is made by adding hydrogen across those double bonds, turning runny oil into a spread. Next time you see unsaturated on a food label, you will know it means C=C!

faq.q: What is the difference between alkanes and alkenes?
faq.a: Alkanes have only single carbon-carbon bonds and are saturated. Alkenes have a carbon-carbon double bond and are unsaturated, so they are more reactive.

faq.q: How do you test for an alkene?
faq.a: Shake it with orange bromine water. An alkene turns it colourless; an alkane leaves it orange.
asks: What is the bromine water test?

faq.a: Saturated means every carbon-carbon bond is single, so the molecule holds as many hydrogen atoms as it can. Unsaturated means there is at least one double bond.

faq.q: What are the general formulas of alkanes and alkenes?
faq.a: Alkanes follow CnH2n+2, like ethane, C2H6. Alkenes follow CnH2n, like ethene, C2H4.
The double bond can open up, letting other atoms, like bromine or hydrogen, add on. Alkanes have no double bond, so they react much less.
asks: Why does ethene react with bromine?

facts: Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2; alkenes have the general formula CnH2n.
Alkenes decolourise bromine water because bromine adds across the C=C double bond.

quiz.why: Propene is an alkene with a C=C double bond.

quiz.say: What is the formula of the alkane with 4 carbon atoms?
quiz.show: What is the formula of the alkane with 4 carbon atoms?
quiz.why: CnH2n+2 with n = 4 gives C4H10, butane.

wrong.2: That is too many hydrogens; each carbon can only make four bonds.
